The calculator prints under valuation.missing: "WACC is not computed: the cost of equity needs a beta and a price: no price series was given: the forward track's price source is Tiingo, and without its token no series is fetched". Under cost_of_capital.missing it prints: "the cost of equity needs a beta and a price: no price series was given: the forward track's price source is Tiingo, and without its token no series is fetched". Three inputs of the discount rate are on record: the risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct}, the equity risk premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium|pct} and the tax rate of {cost_of_capital.tax_rate|pct}. The beta and the market value of equity are both missing for the same reason, so there is no cost of equity, no WACC and nothing to discount at. There is a second gap, and it is on my side. The assumptions.json that Python kept holds no scenario. It dropped bear, base and bull, each because one driver's history note carried a number written in my own words. So even if a price arrived, none of my drivers is on record to run. I state no value and no range.

most_sensitive.assumption: operating margin, year one and year ten

What the record does show is how far this driver has moved. Annual operating margin was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.5.operating_margin|pct} in 2020, the highest of the six years on record. The trailing figure is {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct}, under the three-year average of {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}. The quarter's gross margin, {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.gross_margin|pct}, is the lowest of six quarters. The release lowered its gross margin range for the year while promising improvement in the second half. Anyone choosing the year-ten margin can find support anywhere in that wide range in the company's own record.

most_sensitive.assumption: reinvestment rate, year one and year ten
most_sensitive.reading: Not ranked either, for the same reason. This is the driver the record anchors least. Capital expenditure is missing for the trailing four quarters and for 2023, 2024 and 2025. The company now tags its spending as payments for machinery and equipment, a concept the calculator does not read. The last figure on record is {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.capital_expenditure} in 2022, against operating cash flow that year of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.operating_cash_flow}. The analysts report that half-year payments for machinery and equipment exceed half-year operating cash flow, and the MD&A ties the spending to the Memphis build-out and Tulsa maintenance. Trade working capital rose from {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.trade_working_capital.a_year_earlier} to {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.trade_working_capital.now} over the year. Operating cash flow covers only {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income|pct} of net income. So the company is reinvesting heavily now, by an amount the calculator cannot state. How fast that reinvestment falls back is a choice the record gives no basis for.

accounting_adjustments.reading: No adjustment moved value, for two reasons. First, the accounting reader wrote no adjustment. Its adjustments list is empty, and it gives its reasons for the excess tax benefit, the small bad-debt release and the working-capital build: their amounts are either not fields or already inside operating cash flow. Second, no valuation was computed for any adjustment to move. One gap in the inputs would matter once a valuation runs. The calculator's total debt reads {ratios.solvency.total_debt}, and the cost of debt is set at {cost_of_capital.pre_tax_cost_of_debt|pct} with the note that there is no debt on the balance sheet. This is because the company tags its revolver as a line of credit, which the debt formula does not collect. The MD&A states a drawn revolver balance at June that is above the year-end balance. A bridge from enterprise value to equity value built on the calculator's debt would subtract none of that borrowing, so it would overstate equity value, and the WACC would give debt no weight. Cash is a token {terms.balances_now.cash}, so nothing offsets the borrowing.
